sourceEvidence.label: Commercial client boundary source review at ee06783

assessment.summary: Use a compiled and signed desktop boundary plus service-owned licensing authority; local obfuscation alone remains patchable.

nonNegotiables: Windows x64 is the first release target.
Browser automation and video files remain local.
Production artifacts contain no repository or Python source files.
Release and license private keys never ship.
assumptions: A short offline grace period is acceptable.
No measured latency or memory budget was supplied.

opportunities.title: Replace ambient local authority with a commercial client trust boundary
opportunities.summary: Compile and sign the desktop runtime, authenticate the local channel, and move durable licensing/release authority to a vendor service.
opportunities.diagnosis: Privileged automation is reachable through a fixed unauthenticated loopback API while source, secrets, and runtime artifacts share the deployment model.

evidence.claim: Wildcard CORS and privileged routers have no global desktop-process authentication.
The UI directly calls fixed localhost HTTP and WebSocket endpoints.
Debug and a third-party service secret are source-owned.
No compiled desktop release or signed updater target is defined.
Privileged task routes do not enforce caller identity or entitlements.
Tracked runtime artifacts make repository-copy release construction unsafe.

desiredInvariants: Every privileged operation requires a per-launch local capability and action-appropriate entitlement.
Activation keys are not runtime bearer credentials.
No customer artifact contains source, build secrets, signing keys, or runtime customer data.
Devices can be revoked and minimum safe versions enforced after bounded grace.
Only signed and verified releases execute or install.

options.title: Hardened local client
options.summary: Use Tauri, a compiled sidecar, local API authentication, and an offline signed license while keeping authority on the customer PC.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Per-launch authentication rejects blind calls but remains locally patchable.
Creates a compiled and signed desktop target.

tradeoffs.assessment: Harder static recovery and loopback replay; local checks remain patchable.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Attempt extraction, patching, stale-session replay, and direct route calls.

tradeoffs.assessment: No network task hop, but compiled cold start may change.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare cold start and task-start latency on a clean VM.

tradeoffs.assessment: Tauri and the sidecar add a process and WebView state.
Offline licensing avoids service outages but packaging adds lifecycle modes.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test crash, restart, orphan cleanup, and offline recovery.

tradeoffs.assessment: Signing, installers, and transfers become owned operations.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run a signed release and transfer drill.

tradeoffs.assessment: UI/worker wrapping and authentication coverage are required.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run all UI and automation tests through the package.

residualRisks: Local administrators can patch the verifier.

acceptanceCriteria: No Python source ships and unauthenticated local requests fail.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Withdraw the commercial artifact and retain the developer launcher.

options.title: Hybrid online control plane
options.summary: Keep automation local but centralize activation, entitlements, revocation, device binding, release policy, and selected job capabilities.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Rust-owned per-launch authentication removes ambient loopback authority.
Secrets move to managed services, but exposed material must be rotated.
Central policy evaluates signed leases/capabilities inside use cases.
Clean builds avoid shipping artifacts, but repository cleanup remains required.

tradeoffs.assessment: Durable signing, revocation, and release authority leave the client; the executor remains inspectable.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test revocation, replay, cloning, forgery, bypass, and tampering.

tradeoffs.assessment: Lease renewal can be off-path; selected job capabilities add a request.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure p50/p95 activation, renewal, and protected task start.

tradeoffs.assessment: Client cost resembles the local option, with small caches and managed service state.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure client RSS and service memory per license/job.

tradeoffs.assessment: Grace masks short outages; long outages block new work by policy.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run outage, skew, stale-cache, retry, and grace-extension drills.

tradeoffs.assessment: License, release, audit, key custody, support, and incidents become vendor operations.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Define SLOs and rehearse rotation, revocation, restore, and rollback.

tradeoffs.assessment: All privileged transports and use cases adopt common controls.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Maintain a coverage inventory before enforcement.

residualRisks: A determined attacker can patch a fully local execution path.
Locally decrypted data can be captured.
Long service outages require explicit grace policy.

acceptanceCriteria: Revocation, expiry, limits, stale sessions, cloning, unsigned updates, and tampered binaries fail closed.
migrationNotes: Use audit and warning modes first.
Never interrupt active automation for update.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable remote enforcement while retaining package, local auth, and signed-update controls.

options.title: Cloud-authorized execution
options.summary: Treat the desktop as an untrusted executor and retain proprietary policy plus per-job authority on managed services.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Local auth remains necessary while only the service can mint jobs.
Desktop is compiled/signed and proprietary policy is not distributed.
Protected work requires a scoped server job.

tradeoffs.assessment: Policy that never ships cannot be statically recovered, and clients cannot mint jobs.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Attempt offline job creation, replay, mutation, substitution, and policy extraction.

tradeoffs.assessment: Every protected job adds network, serialization, and scheduling latency.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark p50/p95/p99 task start against a product threshold.

tradeoffs.assessment: Managed queues, caches, and audit state add server memory.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Load-test concurrent authorization and record retained state.

tradeoffs.assessment: The service enters the critical path and needs idempotency, backpressure, failover, and recovery.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run dependency loss, duplicate delivery, delay, failover, and partial-completion tests.

tradeoffs.assessment: The vendor owns always-on jobs, privacy, audit, capacity, and on-call.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Define/test SLOs, alerts, disaster recovery, and deletion.

tradeoffs.assessment: A versioned job state machine and incremental migration are required.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Pilot one action with dual paths and server rollback.

residualRisks: Executor and runtime plans remain observable.

acceptanceCriteria: Modified/offline clients cannot originate valid protected work and service failures recover deterministically.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Return the pilot to hybrid lease authorization.

opportunities.recommendation: Use hybrid control under current local-browser and bounded-offline constraints, with a protocol path to cloud authorization.

openQuestions: Mandatory update behavior during active work
Redistribution rights for browser and extension components
